mashed-potatoes: Can you make mashed potatoes the day before?

Yes. Make them up to a day ahead, cool them quickly in a shallow dish, and refrigerate covered. Reheat with a splash of milk or cream and a little butter, stirring until steaming hot, because chilled potatoes stiffen and dry out.
Why do reheated mashed potatoes turn gluey?
Over-working warm potato starch makes it gluey, and reheating while stirring hard does the same. Warm them gently in a covered dish or on low heat, add liquid first, and fold rather than whip.
What is the best way to reheat mashed potatoes?

Reheat in a covered dish in the oven at about 175°C (350°F), or in the microwave in short bursts, stirring between each. Add milk and butter to restore texture and heat until steaming throughout, 74°C (165°F).
Do instant mashed potatoes last longer than homemade?
Dry instant flakes keep for many months in a sealed pantry container. Once you add water or milk, they behave like homemade mash and need the same short fridge window.
Why do frozen mashed potatoes turn watery?
Ice crystals break the potato cells, so water separates on thawing. Mash made with plenty of butter, cream or cream cheese freezes better; stir well while reheating and the texture mostly comes back.
Can you leave mashed potatoes in a slow cooker to keep warm?
Yes, on the warm setting, as long as they stay above 60°C (140°F). Stir now and then, add a little milk if they dry out, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours of turning it off.
nutella: Does Nutella need to be refrigerated?
No. Ferrero recommends storing Nutella at a cool room temperature, away from heat and sunlight. The fridge makes it hard and difficult to spread without improving its shelf life.
Why did my Nutella go hard?
Cold is the usual cause: the oils in hazelnut and palm fat firm up in a cool kitchen or the fridge. Leave the jar at room temperature for a few hours and it softens again.
Why is there oil on top of my Nutella?
A thin layer of oil can separate when the jar sits warm for a long time. It is harmless; stir it back in. A rancid, paint-like smell is different and means the jar should go.
How can you tell if Nutella has gone bad?
Smell and taste a little: rancid hazelnut fat smells sharp, bitter or like old paint. Mould, a dried-out grainy texture throughout, or a sour taste are also signs to throw it out.
Can you eat Nutella after the best-before date?
Usually yes for a while, if the jar was kept sealed and cool and smells normal. The best-before date is about flavour; the fats slowly turn rancid, so check the smell before eating.
Is it safe to double-dip a knife into Nutella?
A clean, dry knife is fine. Crumbs, butter or moisture from a used knife can bring mould into the jar, so avoid dipping a knife that has touched bread or other food.
chicken-nuggets: Can you cook frozen chicken nuggets without thawing?
Yes. Frozen nuggets are designed to be cooked straight from frozen in the oven, air fryer or fryer. Follow the package time and make sure the centre reaches 74°C (165°F).
Are frozen chicken nuggets fully cooked?
Many are pre-cooked, but some are only browned and still raw inside. Check the package: if it says "uncooked" or "cook thoroughly", treat them like raw chicken and cook to 74°C (165°F).
How do you reheat leftover chicken nuggets so they stay crispy?
Use an air fryer at about 190°C (375°F) for 3 to 5 minutes, or an oven on a rack. The microwave makes the coating soggy. Heat until steaming hot inside.
Only if they thawed in the fridge and were not left out, and expect a softer coating. Cooked nuggets can be frozen once after cooking if they were refrigerated promptly.
Why do some nuggets have a pink centre?
Pink can come from the meat itself or from smoke and cooking chemistry, so colour is not proof. Use a thermometer: 74°C (165°F) in the middle means they are safe.
Can you leave McDonald's or takeaway nuggets in the car?
Not for long. Cooked chicken left between 4 and 60°C (40 and 140°F) should be eaten or refrigerated within 2 hours, or 1 hour when the car or the day is hot.
hot-dogs: Most hot dogs are fully cooked, but they can carry Listeria, which grows slowly in the fridge. Health agencies advise heating them until steaming hot, especially for pregnant women, older adults and young children.
Can you eat hot dogs cold out of the package?
It is common, but not advised for people at higher risk of Listeria. Heating to steaming hot, 74°C (165°F), is the safer habit, and essential for pregnancy.
Why are my hot dogs slimy?
A slimy film usually means spoilage bacteria have grown on the surface. Combined with a sour smell or dull colour, it is a sign to throw the pack out rather than rinse it.
How long can hot dogs sit out at a barbecue?
Cooked hot dogs should not sit out for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 32°C (90°F). Keep extras hot on the side of the grill or cold in a cooler.
How should you store an opened pack of hot dogs?
Wrap the opened pack tightly or move the hot dogs to a sealed bag or container, then keep them in the coldest part of the fridge, not the door.
Can you cook hot dogs from frozen?
Yes. Simmer or grill them from frozen, allowing a few extra minutes, until hot all the way through. Separate them first so they cook evenly.
chia-seeds: They can, but slowly. Chia seeds are rich in omega-3 fats yet have natural antioxidants. Over time they may smell bitter or like old paint; at that point their flavour is gone and they should be replaced.
Should you store chia seeds in the fridge?
Not necessary for whole seeds kept sealed in a cool, dark cupboard. Ground chia goes rancid faster, so keep milled chia in the fridge or freezer.
How long does chia pudding last?
Once mixed with milk or yoghurt, chia pudding is a perishable dairy dish. Keep it covered in the fridge and eat it within a few days; it thickens more as it sits.
How can you tell if chia seeds have gone bad?
Smell them: fresh chia seeds smell of almost nothing. A sour, bitter or musty smell, clumping from moisture, insects or mould mean they should be thrown out.
Yes. Freezing slows rancidity and keeps them for longer. Use an airtight container and let it reach room temperature before opening so condensation does not form.
Do soaked chia seeds need to be refrigerated?
Yes. Once soaked in water, milk or juice, the gel is a moist food that can grow bacteria. Refrigerate it and use it within a few days.
soup: How do you cool a big pot of soup quickly?
Divide it into shallow containers, or set the pot in a sink of iced water and stir. Get it into the fridge within 2 hours; a full hot pot can stay warm in the middle for hours.
Can you put hot soup straight in the fridge?
Yes, in small or shallow containers. Modern fridges handle warm food, and fast cooling is safer than leaving it on the stove. Avoid putting a large, deep pot in whole.
Broths, bean soups, lentil soups and vegetable soups freeze well. Cream soups can separate, and pasta or potatoes go soft, so add those fresh when you reheat.
Is it safe to leave soup out overnight to cool?
No. Soup left out overnight has spent hours in the temperature range where spores of bacteria such as Clostridium perfringens grow. Reheating will not make it safe; throw it out.
How many times can you reheat soup?
Ideally once. Reheat only the portion you will eat, bring it to a rolling boil or 74°C (165°F), and keep the rest in the fridge.
Does homemade soup last longer than canned soup?
Unopened canned soup keeps for years in the pantry. Once opened or made at home, both are perishable and need the same short fridge window.
cooked-pasta: Should you store cooked pasta with or without sauce?
Separately is best: plain pasta tossed with a little oil keeps its texture, and the sauce stays fresher. Pasta already mixed with sauce is fine too, but eat it within the same fridge window.
How do you stop leftover pasta sticking together?
Toss it with a teaspoon of olive oil while still warm, then cool it in a shallow container. To loosen clumps later, dip it briefly in boiling water.
Can cooked pasta make you sick?
Yes, if left warm too long. Bacillus cereus can survive cooking and make toxins in pasta left at room temperature. Refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat until steaming.
How do you reheat cooked pasta without it drying out?
Plunge plain pasta into boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds, or warm sauced pasta in a pan with a splash of water or stock. In the microwave, cover and stir halfway.
Yes. Undercook it slightly, cool, toss with oil and freeze in portions. Baked pasta dishes like lasagne freeze especially well.
Is it safe to eat cold leftover pasta?
Yes, if it was refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking and is within its fridge window. Cold pasta salad is common; the risk comes from how it was cooled, not from eating it cold.
puff-pastry: How do you thaw frozen puff pastry?
Thaw it in the fridge overnight, or at room temperature for about 30 to 40 minutes until it unfolds without cracking. Keep it cold; warm butter makes it sticky and less flaky.
Yes, if it thawed in the fridge and has not been left out. Expect a slightly lower rise, because some layers of butter may have softened.
Why didn't my puff pastry rise?
The butter got too warm, the edges were sealed with egg wash, or the oven was not hot enough. Work quickly, chill shaped pastry before baking, and bake at about 200°C (400°F).
How long does thawed puff pastry last in the fridge?
Use thawed puff pastry within a couple of days. Keep it wrapped tightly so the surface does not dry out or absorb fridge odours.
Can you freeze baked puff pastry?
Yes. Freeze baked pastries once cool, wrapped airtight, and reheat in a hot oven for a few minutes to bring back the crispness.
How can you tell if puff pastry has gone bad?
Grey or dark spots, a sour smell, a slimy surface or freezer burn that has dried the layers mean it is past its best. Mould means it should be thrown out.
salami: Does salami need to be refrigerated?
Whole, dry-cured salami can be kept in a cool, dry place before opening. Once sliced or opened, and for any salami labelled "keep refrigerated", store it in the fridge.
Is the white coating on salami mould?
Often yes, and it is meant to be there: many dry salamis are coated with a harmless white mould that helps the curing. Fuzzy green, black or pink spots are a different matter and mean it should go.
Should you peel the casing off salami?
Peel it if it is a thick or inedible casing, which most dry salamis have. Thin natural casings can be eaten. Keep the casing on the unused end to protect it.
How should you wrap opened salami?
Wrap the cut end in baking paper, then loosely in a bag, and keep it in the fridge. Plastic wrap directly on dry salami can trap moisture and encourage sliminess.
A slimy or sticky surface on sliced salami usually means bacterial spoilage. With a sour or off smell, throw it out.
Health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid cold cured meats like salami unless they are cooked until steaming hot, because of the risk of Listeria and Toxoplasma.
chicken-broth: Can you freeze chicken broth in ice cube trays?
Yes. Freeze broth in ice cube trays or muffin tins, then move the cubes to a freezer bag. They make it easy to add a few spoonfuls to sauces.
Why did my homemade chicken broth turn to jelly?
Gelatine from the bones sets the broth when it cools. It is a sign of a rich stock, not spoilage, and it melts back to liquid when heated.
How long is opened boxed broth good in the fridge?
Treat opened carton broth like homemade: keep it sealed in the fridge and use it within a few days. Freeze what you will not use in time.
How can you tell if chicken broth has gone bad?
A sour smell, cloudiness that was not there before, bubbles or a swollen carton mean it should be thrown out. Do not taste it to check.
Is it safe to leave chicken broth simmering overnight?
Yes, if it stays at a steady simmer the whole time. It is turning off the heat and letting it sit for hours that is unsafe.
Does bone broth last longer than regular broth?
No. Bone broth is just as perishable as any other broth and needs the same fridge window. Its gelatine does not preserve it.
powdered-milk: It lasts a long time, but the fat slowly turns stale. Non-fat dry milk keeps longest; whole milk powder goes rancid sooner because of its fat.
How should you store powdered milk after opening?
Move it to an airtight container, keep it in a cool, dark, dry place and use a dry spoon. Moisture is the main enemy; clumps are the first sign it got in.
How long does reconstituted powdered milk last?
Once mixed with water, it is fresh milk and must be refrigerated. Use it within a few days, as you would an opened carton.
How can you tell if powdered milk has gone bad?
Yellowing, hard clumps, a stale or soapy smell, or an off taste once mixed mean it is past its best. Mould or insects mean throw it out.
You can, but there is little benefit for non-fat powder. For whole milk powder, freezing in an airtight container slows rancidity.
Is expired powdered milk safe to use?
If it was stored sealed and dry and smells and looks normal, it is usually safe, though flavour and nutrients fade. Use it in baking first.
ice-cream: Why does ice cream get icy?
Each time it partly melts and refreezes, small ice crystals grow into large ones. Keep the freezer at -18°C (0°F), put the tub back quickly, and store it at the back, not the door.
How do you stop freezer burn on ice cream?
Press a sheet of baking paper or cling film onto the surface before putting the lid back. Less air contact means fewer ice crystals.
Can you refreeze melted ice cream?
If it melted only slightly and stayed cold, you can refreeze it, but the texture suffers. If it fully melted or sat out more than 2 hours, throw it out.
Can ice cream make you sick?
Rarely, but it can carry Listeria, which survives freezing. Avoid ice cream that has melted and refrozen, and follow any product recalls.
Is homemade ice cream as long-lasting as store-bought?
No. Homemade ice cream has no stabilisers and gets icy within a couple of weeks. If it is made with raw eggs, use a cooked custard base instead.
Where in the freezer should you keep ice cream?
At the back of the main compartment, where the temperature is steadiest. The door warms every time it opens.
pork-rinds: Yes. Once the bag is opened, they absorb moisture and lose their crunch within days. Reseal the bag tightly or move them to an airtight container.
How do you make stale pork rinds crispy again?
Spread them on a tray and bake at about 175°C (350°F) for 3 to 5 minutes, or use an air fryer for a couple of minutes. Let them cool before eating.
Yes. They are fried pork skin, and the fat oxidises over time. A sharp, paint-like or fishy smell means they have gone rancid.
Do pork rinds need to be refrigerated?
No. Unopened or opened bags keep in a cool, dry pantry. The fridge can make them soft.
You can, in an airtight bag, but most people find no need. Freezing does not restore crunch to stale rinds.
Are pork rinds safe after the best-by date?
Usually yes if the bag was sealed and they smell and taste normal. The date is about crunch and flavour.
cooked-rice: Why is leftover rice a food poisoning risk?
Bacillus cereus spores survive cooking. If cooked rice stays warm, they germinate and make a heat-resistant toxin, so reheating won't help. Cool rice quickly and refrigerate it within an hour or two.
How do you cool cooked rice quickly?
Spread it out on a tray or in shallow containers so it loses heat fast, then refrigerate. Aim to have it in the fridge within an hour of cooking.
Is it safe to eat cold rice?
Yes, if it was cooled quickly and kept in the fridge. Cold rice from a properly stored batch is fine in salads and sushi-style bowls.
Can you make fried rice with leftover rice?
Yes, day-old refrigerated rice is ideal because it is drier. Fry it until steaming hot throughout and eat it straight away.
Can you reheat rice in the microwave?
Yes. Sprinkle with water, cover, and heat until steaming hot, stirring halfway. Reheat it only once.
Why does my leftover rice smell sour?
A sour or off smell means bacteria have grown. Throw the rice out; do not taste it to check.
lactose-free-milk: Why does lactose-free milk last longer than regular milk?
Many brands are ultra-pasteurised, heated to a higher temperature, which kills more bacteria. Unopened, it keeps longer in the fridge; once opened, it spoils at a similar rate to regular milk.
Does lactose-free milk need to be refrigerated?
Yes, unless the carton says it is shelf-stable (UHT in aseptic packaging). Once opened, any type must go in the fridge.
Why does lactose-free milk taste sweeter?
The lactase enzyme splits lactose into glucose and galactose, which taste sweeter. It is not a sign of spoilage.
How can you tell if lactose-free milk has gone bad?
Sour smell, thick or lumpy texture, or a curdled look in hot drinks mean it has gone off. Throw it out.
You can, but it may separate and turn grainy after thawing. Shake it well and use it in cooking or smoothies.
Does lactose-free milk go bad faster once opened?
No faster than regular milk. Keep it in the main body of the fridge, not the door, and close the cap tightly.
shrimp: How do you thaw frozen shrimp quickly?
Put them in a colander under cold running water, or seal them in a bag in cold water for 10 to 20 minutes. Cook them right away after cold-water thawing.
How can you tell if raw shrimp has gone bad?
Fresh shrimp smell mildly of the sea. An ammonia or sour smell, slimy texture, or black spots on the flesh mean they should be thrown out.
Are black spots on shrimp safe?
A few black spots on the shell (melanosis) are an enzymatic reaction, not spoilage. Lots of dark patches or any off smell means the shrimp are old.
How long do cooked shrimp last in the fridge?
Cooked shrimp keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge in a sealed container. Shrimp cocktail should go back in the fridge within 2 hours.
Only if they were thawed in the fridge and kept cold. Shrimp thawed in water or the microwave should be cooked before freezing again.
How do you know when shrimp are cooked?
They turn pink and opaque and curl into a loose C shape. A tight O shape usually means they are overcooked.
hummus: Yes, though it may be grainier after thawing. Freeze in small containers with a thin layer of olive oil on top, thaw in the fridge, and stir well.
Why is there liquid on top of my hummus?
Some oil or water separating is normal; stir it back in. A sour, fizzy or fermented smell is a sign of spoilage.
How can you tell if hummus has gone bad?
A sour smell, a tangy fizzy taste, mould or a change in colour mean it should be thrown out. Do not scrape off mould; it spreads through soft dips.
How long does homemade hummus last?
Homemade hummus has no preservatives, so keep it sealed in the fridge and eat it within a few days.
Yes, it adds bacteria to the tub and shortens its life. Spoon out what you need into a bowl.
Can hummus sit out at a party?
Yes, for up to 2 hours, or 1 hour on a hot day. Put out small portions and refill from the fridge.
apple-cider-vinegar: Does apple cider vinegar ever go bad?
Not in a way that makes it unsafe: its acidity prevents harmful bacteria. Over years it can turn cloudier, darker or milder in flavour.
What is the cloudy stuff in apple cider vinegar?
That is the "mother", a harmless mass of cellulose and acetic acid bacteria. It is normal in raw, unfiltered vinegar; you can strain it out.
Does apple cider vinegar need to be refrigerated?
No. Keep it sealed in a cool, dark cupboard. Refrigeration is not needed even after opening.
Can you use apple cider vinegar after the best-by date?
Yes. The date refers to peak quality; vinegar stays safe long after. Check it still smells sharp and acidic.
Why does my apple cider vinegar have sediment?
Sediment is usually bits of the mother or apple solids. It is harmless; shake the bottle or strain it.
Is apple cider vinegar safe for pickling after years?
Use fresh vinegar of at least 5% acidity for safe home pickling. Older vinegar can lose strength.
cut-fruit: How do you stop cut apples from turning brown?
Toss slices with lemon juice, or soak them for a few minutes in salted water or a sugar-water solution, then rinse. Store them airtight in the fridge.
Can you leave cut fruit out at room temperature?
No more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 32°C (90°F). Cut fruit is perishable because bacteria can grow on the exposed flesh.
Which cut fruits last longest in the fridge?
Firm fruits like apples, pears, pineapple and melon keep better than soft fruits like berries, bananas and peaches.
Should you wash fruit before or after cutting?
Before. Rinse whole fruit under running water, even melons with inedible rinds, so the knife does not drag bacteria into the flesh.
Yes, for smoothies and baking. Freeze pieces on a tray, then bag them; the texture is too soft for eating fresh after thawing.
How do you store cut watermelon?
Wrap cut watermelon tightly or store it in a sealed container in the fridge, and use it within a few days.
almonds: Yes. Their oils slowly oxidise, giving a bitter, sharp or paint-like taste. Keep them airtight and cool to slow this down.
Should you store almonds in the fridge or freezer?
Both extend their life compared with the pantry. Use an airtight container so they don't absorb odours, and freeze for the longest storage.
How can you tell if almonds have gone bad?
Smell and taste one: rancid almonds smell sour or like old paint and taste bitter. Shrivelled kernels, mould or insects are other signs.
Do roasted almonds last as long as raw almonds?
Roasted almonds go rancid sooner because heat starts oxidising the oils. Buy smaller amounts or keep them in the fridge.
Does almond flour go bad faster than whole almonds?
Yes. Grinding exposes more surface to air, so almond flour turns rancid faster. Store it in the fridge or freezer.
Can you eat almonds past the best-by date?
Often yes, if they smell and taste fresh. The date is about quality; rancid almonds aren't harmful in small amounts but taste unpleasant.
pumpkin-seeds: Do you need to dry pumpkin seeds before storing them?
Yes. Rinse off the pulp, pat the seeds dry, and air-dry or roast them before storage. Damp seeds go mouldy within days.
How can you tell if pumpkin seeds are rancid?
Rancid pumpkin seeds smell sharp or like oil paint and taste bitter. Discard them; they won't make you seriously ill, but the flavour is ruined.
Yes. Freeze raw or roasted seeds in an airtight bag to slow rancidity. They can go straight from the freezer into recipes.
Are pepitas the same as pumpkin seeds?
Pepitas are hull-less pumpkin seeds, usually from specific pumpkin varieties. Without the shell they go rancid a little faster, so keep them cool and sealed.
Should shelled pumpkin seeds go in the fridge?
The fridge helps in a warm kitchen. Use an airtight jar so they don't pick up odours or moisture.
Can you eat pumpkin seeds from a carved jack-o'-lantern?
Only if you scooped them out right after carving. Seeds from a pumpkin that has sat out for days can carry mould and bacteria.
carrots: Why do carrots go limp in the fridge?
They lose water through their skin. Store them in a sealed bag or container, and cut off leafy tops, which pull moisture out of the root.
How do you revive limp carrots?
Soak them in a bowl of ice-cold water for an hour or two. They absorb water and firm up again, as long as they aren't slimy or mouldy.
Can you store carrots in water?
Peeled or cut carrots keep crisp in a container of water in the fridge. Change the water every couple of days.
What is the white film on baby carrots?
It's "carrot blush", the surface drying out after peeling. It's harmless; a quick soak in cold water removes it.
Do you need to blanch carrots before freezing?
Yes. Blanch sliced carrots for about 2 to 3 minutes, cool them in ice water, dry, and freeze. Unblanched carrots turn woody and lose colour.
Slimy patches, black mould, a sour smell or soft mushy spots mean they should be thrown out. A few small root hairs or bendiness only mean they're drying out.
sesame-seeds: Yes, eventually. Their oil oxidises and they start to smell bitter or like paint. Hulled and toasted seeds go rancid faster than whole seeds.
In a warm or humid kitchen, yes: the fridge or freezer keeps them fresh much longer. Use an airtight container.
Do toasted sesame seeds last as long as raw ones?
No. Toasting starts the oxidation, so toasted seeds lose flavour faster. Toast small batches as you need them.
How do you tell if sesame seeds are bad?
Smell them: fresh seeds smell nutty. A bitter, sour or stale smell, clumps, mould or insects mean they should go.
Does tahini go bad like sesame seeds?
Tahini is ground sesame seeds, so it turns rancid faster than whole seeds once opened. Oil separating on top is normal; a bitter or sour smell is not.
Yes. Freeze them in an airtight container for long storage; they don't clump and can be used straight from frozen.
pepperoni: Does pepperoni need to be refrigerated?
Shelf-stable, dry-cured pepperoni sticks can be kept unopened in the pantry. Once opened, and for sliced pepperoni, keep it in the fridge.
Why is my pepperoni greasy on top of pizza?
Pepperoni releases fat as it heats, which pools in the curled slices. That's normal; blotting with a paper towel removes some of it.
What does bad pepperoni look like?
Slimy slices, a sour or off smell, or fuzzy mould mean it should be thrown out. A white powdery bloom on whole sticks can be salt or harmless mould from curing.
Yes. Freeze them in a flat layer in a bag so you can pull out what you need for pizza, then refreeze the rest.
No. Pepperoni is cured and dried, so it's ready to eat. For people at risk from Listeria, heating until steaming is the safer choice.
How should you store an opened pepperoni stick?
Wrap the cut end in baking paper or plastic wrap and keep it in the fridge. Slice only what you need.
lentils: Do dried lentils ever go bad?
They don't spoil easily, but old lentils get hard, take much longer to cook and may never soften. Insects, mould or a musty smell mean throw them out.
How long do cooked lentils last in the fridge?
Cooked lentils keep about 3 to 5 days in a sealed container in the fridge. Cool them quickly after cooking.
Yes. Freeze cooked lentils in portions with a little cooking liquid; they keep for months and thaw quickly.
Why won't my old lentils soften?
As lentils age, their seed coats harden and absorb water slowly. Hard water and adding acid early also slow cooking. Fresh lentils cook faster.
Do you need to soak lentils?
No. Unlike beans, lentils cook without soaking. Rinse them and pick out any small stones first.
How should you store dried lentils?
In an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. This keeps out moisture and pantry insects.
ground-beef: Why is ground beef brown in the middle?
The inside of a pack isn't exposed to oxygen, so it stays purple-brown. It's normal. Grey or brown all over with a sour smell or slimy feel is spoilage.
What temperature should ground beef be cooked to?
Cook ground beef to 71°C (160°F) in the centre. Colour is not a reliable test; use a food thermometer.
Can you cook frozen ground beef without thawing?
Yes. Cook it in a pan over medium heat, scraping off the browned layer as it thaws. It takes about 50% longer.
Is it safe to eat ground beef that's a little pink?
Only if it reached 71°C (160°F). Grinding spreads surface bacteria through the meat, so ground beef needs to be cooked through, unlike steak.
How long does cooked ground beef last?
Cooked ground beef keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge in a sealed container.
Yes, if it thawed in the fridge and wasn't left out. Expect some loss of texture. Beef thawed in cold water or the microwave should be cooked first.
bacon: Why is my bacon turning grey?
Grey or green-grey colour, slime or a sour smell mean the bacon has spoiled. Fresh bacon is pink with white or cream fat.
How long does cooked bacon last?
Cooked bacon keeps 4 to 5 days in the fridge. Crispy bacon can be frozen in a bag and reheated in a pan or microwave.
Can you cook bacon from frozen?
Yes. Cook it in a pan over low heat, separating slices as they thaw, or bake the frozen block on a tray.
Does bacon need to be cooked?
Yes. Most bacon sold raw needs to be cooked until crisp. Fully cooked bacon is labelled; it only needs reheating.
How should you store opened bacon?
Wrap it tightly in plastic wrap or a zip bag, pressing out air, and keep it in the coldest part of the fridge.
Is bacon grease safe to keep?
Strained bacon grease can be stored in a sealed jar in the fridge for a few months. Throw it out if it smells rancid.
donuts: Do donuts need to be refrigerated?
Plain, glazed or sugared donuts keep at room temperature in a sealed container. Cream- or custard-filled donuts must go in the fridge.
How do you make stale donuts fresh again?
Microwave a donut for 5 to 10 seconds, or warm it in a 175°C (350°F) oven for a few minutes.
Plain and glazed donuts freeze reasonably well, wrapped individually. Cream-filled ones don't; the filling separates.
Why do donuts go stale so fast?
They're small and fried, so they lose moisture and their starch firms up quickly. Store them airtight and eat them within a day or two.
How can you tell if a donut has gone bad?
Mould, a sour smell, or a slimy filling mean it should be thrown out. Stale, hard donuts are safe but unpleasant.
Can you leave Krispy Kreme donuts out overnight?
Glazed donuts can stay at room temperature overnight in their box or a sealed container. Filled donuts should be refrigerated.
whipping-cream: You can freeze it, but it separates and won't whip well after thawing. Use frozen cream in cooking, soups and sauces instead.
How can you tell if whipping cream has gone bad?
A sour smell, lumps, or a yellowish colour mean it has spoiled. Thick cream that pours as clumps is past its best.
Why won't my whipping cream whip?
It's too warm, too low in fat, or past its best. Chill the cream, bowl and whisk, and use cream with at least 30% fat.
How long does whipped cream last in the fridge?
Freshly whipped cream holds for about a day before it starts to deflate. Stabilised cream (with gelatine or mascarpone) lasts longer.
Is heavy cream the same as whipping cream?
Heavy cream has more fat (about 36%+) than whipping cream (about 30–35%). Both whip; heavy cream holds peaks longer.
Can you use whipping cream past the date?
If it was kept cold and smells and tastes fresh, yes, for a short time. Ultra-pasteurised cream often lasts longer than its date once unopened.
aioli: Homemade aioli with raw egg yolk carries a risk of Salmonella. Use pasteurised eggs, keep it refrigerated and eat it within a few days.
Is store-bought aioli the same as mayonnaise?
Many store aiolis are garlic mayonnaise made with pasteurised eggs and preservatives, so they last longer than homemade.
No. Aioli is an emulsion and separates into oil and liquid when frozen.
How can you tell if aioli has gone bad?
